title: gtm-cs-1on1-prep-samira-patel-aaron-li-2026-04-02
content:
1:1 prep: Aaron Li (AE) — 2026-04-02
Owner: Samira Patel (CSM)
Duration: 30 min
Customer: ACME Corp (Enterprise tier) — main contact: Claire Huang (PM)
Goal for this 1:1: surface blockers for current rollout, agree next delivery milestones, clarify eligibility for Dedicated discounts, align on Q2 success metrics.

Agenda (approx):
- 0-5m quick personal check-in + wins
  - Aaron: closed upsell with BetaRetail; Samira: triaged data pipeline issue for ACME
- 5-12m account health and usage signals
  - Last 2 weeks: 3.2M tokens/month (up 18%) but CPU throttling spikes on weekday mornings (08:00-10:00 PT)
  - Errors: 1.1% rate on streaming responses tied to a model variant fallback (see CS-789)
  - Latency: p50 stable at 180ms, p95 spiking to 750ms during throttling windows
- 12-20m rollout status / blockers
  - ACME integration with private deployment: network team waiting on IP allowlist confirmation from their security (blocked since 2026-03-25)
  - Aaron flagged that billing team needs a committed capacity quote to finalize procurement (deadline 2026-04-09)
  - Action needed: confirm Dedicated discount tier and timeline
- 20-28m success metrics + next milestones
  - Proposed Q2 success metrics: latency p95 < 300ms, error rate < 0.5%, cost-per-1k-tokens <= $0.85 after optimization
  - Proposed milestones: IP allowlist confirmation (by 2026-04-06), Dedicated quote delivered (2026-04-05), canary rollout of private deployment (target 2026-04-20)
- 28-30m wrap + confirm owners and dates

Prep notes / things to surface in meeting:
- Bring the Dedicated pricing matrix and a draft committed capacity SKUs PDF (refer to internal pricing deck). Be ready to propose a 6- or 12-month commit with step-down clauses.
- Engineering note: SRE has a mitigation (short-term) to reduce p95 spikes by shifting autoscale warm-up; needs customer approval for brief traffic shaping during business hours.
- Risk signals: procurement timeline slipping, security team slow on allowlist. If both slip >2 weeks, churn risk moves to "moderate".
- Play to win: offer a 30-day pilot of Dedicated with a credit against first invoice to accelerate procurement (subject to finance approval).

Open tickets / references (quick):
- CS-789: Streaming fallback error analysis (linked)
- ENG-1421: Autoscaler warm-up improvement (PR pending review)
- PAY-214: Draft committed capacity pricing (internal doc)

Proposed talking points / phrasing:
- "Claire, we want to remove blockers this sprint — if we can get the allowlist confirmed by next Monday our engineering team can begin the private rollout and keep your latency under the target. What support do you need from us to speed that up?"
- "We can offer a short committed pilot and credit to help procurement evaluate Dedicated without delaying integration. Would that help on your side?"

Action items (to assign in meeting):
- Aaron: follow up with ACME procurement to confirm decision timeline and share draft committed capacity SKUs (due 2026-04-05)
- Samira: escalate allowlist ask to ACME security (intro email + 1-pager on required IPs) and confirm network contact (due 2026-04-03)
- Eng (SRE): schedule 30-minute call to review autoscaler mitigation and traffic-shaping plan with ACME (tentative 2026-04-06) — Samira to coordinate
- Finance: prepare pilot credit proposal for internal signoff (due 2026-04-04) — Aaron to loop in finance

Notes to self (post-meeting follow-up checklist):
- Send meeting notes + agreed dates within 24 hours
- Create JIRA sub-tasks for each action and link to CS-789
- Prep technical runbook for canary private rollout (screenshot templates, rollback steps)
- Confirm internal owners for SLA monitoring after rollout (SRE oncall + account playbook)

Misc scratchpad (short snippets):
- If allowlist delayed >1 week, offer temporary hosted routing to a Dedicated-equivalent model to reduce latency impact
- Check earlier demo recording (2026-02-18) for Claire's commented preferences on structured outputs

End of notes.
